title: Best Smartwatches and Fitness Watches UK
short: Fitness and sports watches compared by GPS accuracy, heart rate tracking and battery life, from budget training watches to premium adventure watches.
intro: The right fitness watch depends heavily on what you train for: runners want accurate GPS and pace metrics, while heart rate accuracy or battery life matter more for others. This guide compares watches tested by Men's Fitness, whose team of tech journalists tested 10 watches for running, training and health tracking.

products.name: Forerunner 970
products.best_for: Serious runners who want Garmin's full training and recovery insights
products.key_spec: AMOLED touchscreen, up to 26hrs GPS / 15 days battery
products.summary: Men's Fitness's overall pick, with a crisp AMOLED touchscreen and new running metrics on top of Garmin's market-leading training and recovery insights. Battery life drops slightly from the previous Forerunner 965, and the new running metrics need an additional accessory.
pros: Great tracking performance for runs and more
cons: New running metrics require an additional accessory
Shorter battery life than the previous Forerunner 965

products.name: Pace 4
products.best_for: Beginners who want serious training tools at a low price
products.key_spec: AMOLED, up to 41hrs GPS / 19 days battery
products.summary: Men's Fitness calls this brilliant all-round value, with advanced tools like Race Predictor, Virtual Pacer and blood oxygen monitoring rarely found this cheap, plus reliable multi-band GPS and great battery life. The design feels a bit plastic and basic, and heart rate measurements were patchy in testing.
pros: Great battery life for the price

products.name: Vantage V3
products.best_for: Buyers who prioritise reliable heart rate data above all else
products.key_spec: AMOLED, multiband GPS, Gen 4 heart rate sensor
products.summary: Men's Fitness found this delivered one of the most reliably accurate heart rate measurements of any watch tested, with a bright AMOLED display and free Strava and Komoot subscriptions included. Phone pairing and syncing was buggy in testing, and there's no Spotify or Deezer playback.
pros: Free Komoot and Strava subscriptions included
cons: Phone pairing and syncing can be buggy

products.name: Race 2
products.best_for: Buyers who want strong GPS battery life across many sports
products.key_spec: 1.5in LTPO AMOLED, up to 65hrs GPS / 18 days battery
products.summary: Men's Fitness's top Suunto pick, with over 100 sport modes, dual-frequency GPS, offline maps and routing, plus a bigger, brighter display than the original Race. Training insights can feel complicated, and there's no offline music support.
pros: Bigger, brighter display than its predecessor
Dual-frequency GPS with offline maps and routing

products.name: Watch Fit 4 Pro
products.best_for: Buyers who like the Apple Watch style without the price
products.key_spec: AMOLED, 40m dive-grade water resistance, up to 10 days battery
products.summary: A robustly built alternative for buyers who want a fitness-focused smartwatch without Apple pricing, with a titanium bezel, sapphire glass and over 15,000 golf courses mapped, plus real-time dive tracking. Men's Fitness found GPS and heart-rate accuracy can waver, and it's less customisable than some smartwatches.
pros: Robust titanium and sapphire glass construction
cons: GPS and heart-rate accuracy can waver

products.name: Watch 3
products.best_for: Buyers who don't want to charge their watch every couple of days
products.key_spec: AMOLED, up to 120hrs GPS / 7 days battery
products.summary: Men's Fitness highlights market-leading battery life at up to five days in GPS mode, built with a stainless steel case, sapphire crystal display and titanium alloy bezel, at a price under £320. It has a big face that may not suit smaller wrists and is a little weighty.
pros: Premium stainless steel and sapphire crystal build
Strong value for the feature set
cons: Large face may not suit smaller wrists
A little heavy on the wrist

products.name: Watch Ultra 3
products.best_for: Buyers who want the best all-round smartwatch experience with fitness credentials
products.key_spec: Retina LTPO OLED, 3000 nits peak, up to 72hrs GPS battery
products.summary: Men's Fitness's pick for buyers who want smartwatch features alongside fitness tracking, with a wider screen than the Ultra 2, satellite connectivity for off-grid situations, and improved battery life and charging speed. Fitness tracking itself isn't hugely different from the Ultra 2, and it still won't last a full week without charging.
pros: Wider, brighter screen for outdoor visibility
Improved battery life and faster charging
cons: Fitness tracking not hugely different from the Ultra 2
Still needs charging within a week

products.name: Grit X2 Pro
products.best_for: Buyers who want a rugged watch for off-grid exploring
products.key_spec: AMOLED, dual-frequency GPS, offline maps, up to 30hrs GPS battery
products.summary: Men's Fitness's top adventure pick, built to handle training, racing and off-grid exploring with a punchy AMOLED display, accuracy-enhancing dual-frequency GPS and offline maps with Strava route sync. App connectivity was flaky in testing, and it's lighter on general smartwatch features.
pros: Long battery life for an adventure watch

guide.q: Do I need a dedicated fitness watch or would a regular smartwatch do?
guide.a: A dedicated fitness watch, like the Garmin or COROS models here, typically offers more accurate GPS, longer battery life and deeper training and recovery insights. A general smartwatch like the Apple Watch Ultra 3 covers fitness well too, but usually needs more frequent charging and leans more toward everyday smartwatch features.

guide.q: How much does wrist-based heart rate accuracy vary?
guide.a: It varies more than most buyers expect, and no wrist sensor is as accurate as a chest strap. If heart rate accuracy is a priority, a watch specifically praised for it, like the Polar Vantage V3 here, is worth prioritising over one with only average results.

guide.q: What battery life should I expect in GPS mode versus everyday use?
guide.a: GPS tracking drains battery much faster than everyday smartwatch use, so a watch's advertised multi-day battery life usually assumes GPS is off. If you do long GPS-tracked activities regularly, check the specific GPS battery life figure, which can range from under a day to several days depending on the watch.

guide.q: Is multiband or dual-frequency GPS worth having?
guide.a: Multiband or dual-frequency GPS, found on watches like the Polar Vantage V3 and Suunto Race 2 here, improves accuracy in tricky conditions like dense cities or under tree cover, at some cost to battery life. It's most valuable for runners who train in built-up areas or woodland trails.
